note: Iceland: EEA and Swiss nationals live and work freely (the eea list). Artists, except musicians employed to perform in restaurants, are exempt from the work permit for up to 90 days per calendar year (taken as 90 within 365), provided the work is notified no later than the day it begins, each time; beyond that, a work permit and residence permit (island.is, the Directorate of Immigration). The exemption is the Act on Foreigners' Right to Work's art. 23, whose 90 days a year island.is gives, and the Directorate of Labour's notification form for work of under 90 days names artists among its kinds of exemption (both read 2026-11-04). Regulation 339/2005, art. 4(b), exempts artists for four weeks a year: that is the regulation's one version, in force since 30 March 2005, while the Act as the Government's channels give it now sets 90 days, and the Act outranks the regulation, so the 90 days stand. The Act itself wasn't read: althingi.is answers this client with a Cloudflare check, not passed.

sources.title: Ísland.is, Short-term residence permit: Rights and obligations
sources.said: The following foreign nationals are exempt from the requirement to obtain a work permit for employment in Iceland for up to 90 days per calendar year: ... Artists, with the exception of musicians employed to perform in restaurants. ... It is necessary to notify the authorities of work carried out under this exemption no later than the same day the work begins, on each occasion.

sources.title: Ísland.is, Sækja um atvinnuleyfi: Undanþága vegna skammtímavinnu undir 90 dögum á ári
sources.said: Undanþága vegna skammtímavinnu undir 90 dögum á ári Í vissum tilvikum geta störf útlendinga fallið undir undanþágu í lögum ef starfstímabil fer ekki yfir 90 daga á ári. Fari starfstímabil hins vegar yfir 90 daga þarf að sækja um og fá útgefið atvinnuleyfi. Frekari upplýsingar um þessa undanþágu eru í grein 23 í lögum um atvinnuréttindi útlendinga.
